SLIDE 02 / 06 • THE STRATEGIC IDEA

Stop selling "bus hire." Sell production uptime and duty-of-care insurance.

In Nigeria, enterprise transportation is not an administrative errand—it is an operational risk control center. When an employee bus breaks down, an entire production line or retail shift collapses.

THE OLD INFORMAL MODEL

Ad-hoc negotiations with individual bus drivers, mechanical breakdowns with no standby vehicles, informal cash vouchers, zero IVMS telematics, and high passenger risk.

THE NETS DRIVE MODEL

Audited corporate fleet contracts, guaranteed 15-minute replacement SLAs, real-time GPS tracking, defensive-driving certified captains, and predictable monthly corporate invoicing.

SLIDE 04 / 06 • THE 3-STAGE FUNNEL

Educate • Engage • Convert

1. TOFU (Months 1–2)

Agitate the Hidden Cost: Highlight the true cost of unmanaged transit (lost production hours, employee churn post-fuel subsidy hike, safety liability).

2. MOFU (Months 3–6)

Establish Operational Authority: Demonstrate our telematics dashboard, 15-minute vehicle backup SLA, route clustering science, and driver screening standards.

3. BOFU (Months 7–9)

De-Risk Conversion: Offer 14-day to 30-day pilot routes, TCO audits, and pre-negotiated Master Service Agreements (MSAs) with guaranteed punctuality penalties.
